faqBestA: In our published dataset, the {place} location has the highest Goods Score ({score, number} out of 100). The score uses neighborhood Census measures to help compare locations. It does not measure store inventory, customer reviews, or donation quality.
faqScoreQ: How does Thriftly rank Goodwill stores in {city}?
faqScoreA: Each store gets a 0 to 100 Goods Score built from four U.S. Census measures of the area within about three miles: median home value, household income, share of college graduates, and median rent. Stores with wealthier surrounding neighborhoods score higher.
faqCountQ: How many Goodwill locations are in {city}?
faqCountA: Thriftly lists {count, plural, one {# Goodwill store} other {# Goodwill stores}} within {radius, number} miles of {city}, using published store data from AllThePlaces and OpenStreetMap. Listings may be missing or outdated, so coverage can be incomplete.

outletIntro: Looking for a Goodwill outlet, often called “the bins”? Start with these two Los Angeles-area locations listed on Goodwill Southern California’s outlet page.
outletSource: Source checked November 4, 2026. This is a selected operator-sourced guide, not a complete list of every outlet in the region.
operatorBody: Check current hours, prices and shopping rules on the operator’s website. Local policies can change, and this guide does not promise today’s inventory or a particular price.
regularBody: The city guide lists mapped Goodwill locations with directions and neighborhood scores. Outlet merchandise and regular-store inventory can differ; the score does not predict what you will find at either.
methodDescription: Understand the Goods Score: Census measures, weights, data dates and limitations. A neighborhood score is not a store review or an inventory forecast.
methodIntro: The Goods Score is a 0 to 100 comparison of the neighborhoods around a store. It helps you choose places to explore. It does not measure merchandise, donation quality, prices or customer satisfaction.
catchment: We use Census tracts whose center points lie within {radius, number} miles of the store. Each measure is averaged using population and distance: more populous, closer tracts contribute more. This is a geographic approximation, not a study of who donates to that store.
normalization: Each measure is normalized against fixed ranges in our open-source model. Home value uses a logarithmic scale. Missing measures contribute zero, so a low score can reflect missing data. A score of 80 is not an 80th-percentile ranking or an 80% chance of finding something.
dataBody: The scoring model uses the 2022 American Community Survey five-year estimates. Published store data comes from AllThePlaces and OpenStreetMap. AllThePlaces publishes its data under CC0; OpenStreetMap data has its own attribution and license requirements.
refresh: Refreshes are attempted weekly. If a source fails validation, the last complete published file stays in use; a schedule does not guarantee weekly updates.
verify: Use it to plan, then verify
verifyBody: Coverage can miss stores or include outdated listings. Check the operator’s website before traveling. Inventory changes, and a neighborhood score cannot tell you what a store has today. Thriftly is an independent project and is not affiliated with Goodwill.
